one_liner: Website builder platform with REST APIs for merchant commerce data.
blocker: API keys require a Commerce Advanced paid plan; OAuth client registration requires Squarespace review before credentials are issued.

evidence.claim: Commerce API requests authenticate via a generated API key or OAuth 2.0 client registration.
evidence.quote: Depending on your development needs, you can use a generated API key or start the OAuth process with Squarespace to become a registered OAuth client.

evidence.claim: Generating an API key for a custom application requires the Commerce Advanced plan (paid).
evidence.quote: With [Squarespace's Commerce Advanced](https://www.squarespace.com/pricing) plan, you can develop a custom application for a Squarespace merchant site.

evidence.claim: OAuth client credentials are issued only after Squarespace reviews the registration.
evidence.quote: We will review your registration and respond with `your_client_id` and `your_client_secret` as soon as possible.

evidence.claim: Commerce APIs are REST-style over HTTPS with standard verbs and status codes.
evidence.quote: All Commerce APIs are built on HTTPS and designed with REST principles in mind.

evidence.claim: API surface spans roughly nine resource families including orders, products, inventory, contacts, discounts, transactions, analytics, and webhooks.
evidence.quote: **Webhook Subscriptions API:** Subscribe to notifications from a site, like when an order was created, by configuring a webhook endpoint.

notes: Profiles API is in maintenance mode ('new integrations should use the Contacts API'). Webhook Subscriptions API is OAuth-only. API keys never expire while the site is active. No official Squarespace MCP server; a third-party community MCP exists (github.com/BusyBee3333/squarespace-mcp-2026-complete), and the 'Square MCP server' result is from Square (squareup), a different company.
